payload.text: SAFETY/ORACLE — gk_price is the independent golden reference (the Garman-Kohlhagen two-rate FX vanilla closed form) against which the production engine is validated, NOT the engine's own pricer: for t>0 it computes d1=(ln(S/K)+(r_dom-r_for+0.5*vol^2)*t)/(vol*sqrt(t)), d2=d1-vol*sqrt(t), df_dom=e^{-r_dom*t}, df_for=e^{-r_for*t}, and returns S*df_for*N(d1)-K*df_dom*N(d2) for a Call (put by symmetry); for t<=0 it returns the discounted intrinsic max(sign*(S-K),0). It deliberately re-derives the price from first principles with its own norm_cdf so a parity test (e.g. vanilla_price_and_greeks_match_quantlib, also pinned to published QuantLib numbers) can disagree with the engine — the anti-circular-oracle property: numerical correctness is checked against this reference, never merely asserted plausible. Pure: it reads only its scalar args and returns the f64 price, mutating nothing.
